FOUND 2026-08-20 by running the loop honestly rather than by looking for it: epoch:the-declared-walls-hold was set arrived with BOTH its capabilities delivered, and arrival_delta reported BOTH as `outstanding`.

=== THE MECHANISM, read from the source and not inferred ===

crates/reflow2-core/src/temporal.rs, item_is_delivered:

    node::CAPABILITY => Ok(self.capability_is_realized(item_id)?
                        && self.capability_has_evidence(item_id)?)

and capability_is_realized (detect.rs) is: an Artifact REALIZES the capability, OR an Artifact realizes a Component the capability is ALLOCATED_TO.

So delivery requires A FILE ON DISK. `Capability.status` is never consulted. Verification evidence alone is not enough - measured directly: a capability at status `realized` WITH a passing system-level Verification attached still came back `outstanding`, because the AND requires both halves and the artifact half cannot be satisfied by a check.

=== WHY THIS IS NOT 'JUST SET THE STATUS' ===

The governing doctrine is right and should not be weakened: delivery is COMPUTED from the golden thread, never asserted, and there is deliberately no `achieved` modality, because a plan that records its own success is a plan lying about itself. The defect is not that delivery is computed. It is that the computation admits exactly ONE kind of evidence - an artifact - while reflow2 itself models several.

=== WHAT IT COSTS AN ARBITRARY USER'S PROJECT ===

A large share of real increment content produces NO NEW FILE:
  · a re-decomposition, or any boundary change
  · a retirement - something correctly leaving the design
  · a governance decision, an accepted rule, a settled question
  · a correction to a model that was wrong about the world

Every one of those sits `outstanding` forever. And `outstanding` is DEFINED as 'still pointed here, not delivered, and nobody has said which of deferred or discontinued it is - that is the question to put to the user'. So the tool asks the user a question about work that is finished, and keeps asking. A plan that cannot mark model work delivered will, increment after increment, accumulate a backlog of phantom incompletions - and the natural response is to stop scheduling model work, which is precisely the work systems engineering is FOR.

It bites hardest on exactly the modularization and black-box work reflow2 is meant to support, because almost all of that is model change.

=== A SECOND TENSION, IN THE SAME REPLY ===

arrival_delta also said: 'nothing is scheduled `required` ... so there is no obligation to miss and it is NOT ready to cut. An increment that promises nothing has not been scoped.' That is a fair criticism. But the plan-increments skill instructs the opposite - `required` is the scheduling face of a KPP, so 'ask, never assume' - and this plan used `expected` BECAUSE THE SKILL SAID TO. A user following reflow2's own guidance therefore builds an increment reflow2 then reports as unscoped and never ready to cut. Two pieces of correct guidance, in tension, with no way for the follower to satisfy both.

=== STATED HONESTLY: NOT ACTED ON ===

The epoch is being LEFT reporting `outstanding`. Editing the plan to match what happened is what the skill forbids, and the false reading is itself the evidence. This is recorded for Anthony's decision, not fixed.
